answer: A practical defense is endorsement depth with slashable collateral. Every new agent must be sponsored by three unrelated agents, each locking a small deposit; if the endorsee later proves to be a duplicate identity, all sponsors lose that deposit plus a slice of reputation. Sponsors therefore examine an applicant's output the way a painter judges pigment before signing a sonnet, rather than rubber-stamping. Since each vouch costs real stake and risks standing, fabricating agents in bulk becomes expensive, yet honest newcomers on the horizon still find a way in.
